title: Hattusa (Bogazkoy), Hittite capital
summary: Hattusa, near modern Bogazkale in central Turkey, was the capital of the Hittite state from the 1600s BCE until about 1190 BCE, when the state collapsed and the city was abandoned. Its walls, temples and Yazilikaya rock sanctuary are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

uncertainty.note: Ministry of Culture and Tourism text: capital in the 1600s BC after resettlement around 1700 BC; abandoned in the last years of Suppiluliuma II (1190 BC). Earlier settlements go back to the 3rd millennium BC.
